messages:
Marcus: Quick sync — postmortem follow-up for the 3/21 inference latency spike. Need to lock owners, timelines, and any SLO tweaks we recommend to management.
Elena: I pulled the timeline and error-budget burn. p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~270ms during the window, p99 to ~1.2s. Error budget for the week is ~78% consumed across prod clusters.
Avery: Was the root cause the microbatching regression or the new kernel fallback?
Samir: Looks like both. Batch sizing regressed after the runtime change; fallback routing also retried a lot which amplified queue depth.
Elena: Proposed short list: 1) revert microbatching tweak on canary, 2) tighten routing fallback to prefer lower-latency variants, 3) dashboard + alert improvements for recurring tail spikes.
Marcus: Ok. Let's assign concrete owners and deadlines. We should avoid changing committed SLOs unless we have to; ops can propose temporary SLA grace but we need PM sign-off.
Avery: I'll take the microbatch revert and test plan. ETA: 48h for canary revert + 4 days for validation across regions. Owner: Avery.
Samir: I'll own routing policy adjustments (limit retry amplification, add jitter). ETA: 72h for safe rollout and canary. Owner: Samir.
Elena: I'll build the dashboard tiles: per-model p95/p99 by region, error-budget burn rate over time, and an alerts heatmap for repeated regression patterns. ETA: EOD Friday. Owner: Elena.
Marcus: I'll draft the SLO status note for leadership and legal (we'll keep SLOs but mark a mitigated incident). ETA: 1 week. Owner: Marcus.
SRE-Bot: Incident link: <https://redwood.incidents/INC-2026-2148|INC-2026-2148> — severity: sev2 — reopened 2026-03-21T03:12Z.
Samir: Action: add a recurrence detector that flags the same topology/model hitting p99 > 1s two times in 7 days. Will prototype and attach to the alerting pipeline. ETA: 6 days.
Avery: Quick note on validation: we need a unit to measure effective batch size distribution after revert. I can add a smoke check to the canary that asserts median batch size within expected range.
Elena: For dashboards, building a widget that surfaces per-route queue-time vs execution-time helps differentiate queuing vs kernel slowness.
Marcus: For SLO governance: propose we keep p95 at 150ms, but temporarily relax p99 SLO alerting thresholds for 72h during remediation so oncall isn't paged repeatedly. PM sign-off required — I'll ping @PM-Team.
Elena: +1 for temporary alert suppression if we maintain visibility. We should still capture every occurrence in the dashboards.
Samir: Will ensure retries are counted separately in metrics so error-budget math doesn't double-count.
Avery: One more: add a rollout playbook step to disable new runtime flags for a model family in under 30m. I can draft. ETA: 3 days.
Marcus: Summarize owners and deadlines: 
- A1 revert microbatching: Avery — 48h canary, 4d validation
- A2 routing retries & jitter: Samir — 72h rollout
- A3 dashboards & alerts: Elena — EOD Friday
- A4 SLO status note: Marcus — 1 week
- A5 recurrence detector prototype: Samir — 6 days
- A6 rollout playbook + smoke: Avery — 3 days
Marcus: Please react with :thumbsup: when you accept. We'll reconvene in 24h to check progress.
Avery: :thumbsup: accepted.
Samir: :thumbsup: accepted.
Elena: :thumbsup: accepted.
SRE-Bot: Reminder scheduled: follow-up check-in in 24h (1732196399).
Marcus: I'll also add a short note to the SLO doc listing the incident and keeping a timeline of remediation steps — helps for future postmortems.
Elena: One risk callout: if we keep routing stricter, we might push load to fewer GPUs temporarily; I'll monitor capacity dashboards and raise if we need short-term scaling.
Samir: Agreed — I'll coordinate with infra autoscaling.
Marcus: Great. If anyone hits blockers, ping here or DM. Closing thread for now, will reopen on the 24h check-in.
